title: Final letters
hookLine: five letters change shape at the end of a word

lines: MELECH: A KAF AT THE END.
cards: Melech. King. Three letters: mem, lamed, kaf.
At the start of a word, kaf is a rounded shape that sits on the line, like the cupped palm from a few days back.
At the end of melech it straightens, and its tail drops below the line, as if the word were stepping off a curb. Same letter, same sound, new shape. And kaf isn't alone.
Mem, which you met in mayim, does it too, and so do nun, peh and tzadi. The Talmud groups the five under one made-up word, mantzepach, built from the letters themselves.

teach.b: Sofit means final, from sof, end. A mem sofit is a final mem.

teach.h: A CLOSED BOX AND FOUR LONG TAILS.
teach.b: Four things to know. First, the shapes. Final mem closes into a box.
Final kaf, nun, peh and tzadi drop a long tail below the line, as if leaning into the space after the word. Second, the seers.

teach.h: THE SEERS SPOKE THEM, THE TALMUD SAYS.
teach.b: The Talmud, in tractate Shabbat, says the final forms were spoken by the tzofim, the watchmen or seers. Then it raises a puzzle: if the Torah was given with them, how could later people have introduced them?
Its answer: they were known, then forgotten, then restored. The rabbis cared enough about the shape of an ending to argue where it came from. Third, the bent and the straight.
On the same page, the Talmud reads nun and tzadi as pairs.

teach.h: BENT NOW, STRAIGHT AT THE END.
teach.b: A bent nun and a straight nun: a person faithful when bent low will be faithful standing straight. A bent tzadi and a straight tzadi: the same for the righteous.
Remember the nun that fell in Ashrei, and the tzadi of Noah in his generations. Here they get a second shape, upright at the end. Fourth, the week.
It began with peh, the mouth, and Moses slow of speech.

Then tzadi, the righteous one; kuf, holy; resh, the head of the year; shin on the doorpost; tav, the seal of truth; and now the endings. Two of this week's letters, peh and tzadi, have a final form of their own.
In Hebrew, how a word ends shows on the page.

how: Hebrew writes five letters, kaf, mem, nun, peh and tzadi, in a final form (sofit) at the end of a word; the Talmud groups them under the made-up word mantzepach and discusses them in Shabbat 104a.

o: the final form a letter takes at the end of a word
a dot that tells you how to say a letter's vowel
a letter that goes silent when it ends a word

p: a word to remember the five

s: every Hebrew letter has a final form
only five: kaf, mem, nun, peh and tzadi.
final mem is closed, while the other four final forms stretch below the line
mem closes into a box; the others drop a long tail.
the Talmud says the final forms were spoken by the seers
then asks how that fits the Torah, and answers: known, forgotten, restored.

games.q: you're writing melech, king, in Hebrew. you reach the last letter, a kaf. which shape do you write?
o: the rounded kaf, the same as at the start of a word.
the final kaf, with its tail dropping below the line.
games.why: at the end of a word, kaf straightens and drops its tail below the line: kaf sofit.

practice: With a pen, or a fingertip on your palm, draw a final nun: one straight stroke from the top down, past where the line would be, slowly, all the way.

Then think of one thing ending in your life this week, a project, a season, a habit, a hard stretch, and ask whether you'd like it to end closed and complete like a final mem, or upright and reaching on like that nun.
If you pray, you can bring it in.

wordCard.voice: Sofit. Final: the end form of five letters, kaf, mem, nun, peh and tzadi. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: final — the end form of a letter, from sof, end.

carryVoice: Your line: five endings. An ending can stand up straight. A week of letters, done.
